purpose: Relative hourly domestic electricity consumption for a single-rate customer, used to weight the hourly PyPSA clearing price into a household-shaped energy cost.
method: Ofgem base/peak demand allocation converted to an hourly shape: baseload product covers every hour at base_share/H, the peak product adds peak_share/P during the Elexon peak block. Normalised to sum to one.
limitations: Two blocks only. It reproduces Ofgem's own shaping input, not an Elexon Profile Class 1 half-hourly regression, so within-block structure such as the domestic evening peak after 19:00 is absent.
No seasonal variation: the 2020 cap periods declare one base/peak allocation, so the shape is flat across months and only varies by day type and hour.
Applied to model snapshots by day-of-week and local hour, and by calendar date only for England and Wales bank holidays (off-peak), because the profile's only structure is the peak block.

source.dataset: Default tariff cap model, Annex 2 wholesale, base and peak demand allocation
source.peak_block_definition: Elexon/EFA peak block: 07:00-19:00 Monday to Friday, London local time, England and Wales bank holidays excluded
